title: Orchestrated residency guardrails and forced switchover evidence pipeline
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers require provable guarantees that data never leaves prescribed jurisdictions. Current failover logic prioritizes availability over locality and can trigger automatic regional switchover to standby regions that do not satisfy customer residency constraints. There is no automated evidence bundle produced when a failover is performed, making post-incident attestations manual and slow.

Goal: Implement orchestration-level residency guardrails that: (1) prevent automatic cross-jurisdiction failover unless an explicit policy allows it or a manual approval step is taken; (2) generate a tamper-evident evidence bundle for any residency-impacting actions (evacuation, switchover, snapshot export) including signed route traces, model variant identifiers, retention settings, and KMS key IDs; (3) allow operators to configure a quarantine window and controlled grace-switched standby that preserves residency in all cases; (4) integrate with the audit reporting pipeline so legal/compliance teams receive machine-readable proofs and human-readable playbooks.

Proposed design (high level):
- Residency policy evaluation service (RPE): a lightweight policy engine that evaluates request-level residency constraints against candidate failover targets. Runs as part of Smart Routing.
- Failover gating: introduce a new failover state machine that supports: ALLOW, BLOCK, PROMPT (requires human approval via Console), and QUARANTINE (degrade service but keep data pinned to original region).
- Evidence bundle generator: on any state transition that affects residency, collect: request traces, routing decisions, model version, container image digests, infra instance IDs, KMS key fingerprint, timestamped signed manifest. Bundle is SHA256-signed by a cluster HSM-backed key and stored in encrypted long-term evidence store (S3 with object lock + KMS). Index and push metadata to the audit pipeline.
- Retention enforcement: tie evidence bundles to retention policy; flag retention mismatches as security violations to be surfaced in Console and via webhook to downstream compliance systems.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict-block policy improves compliance but increases MTTR and reduces availability; mitigation: allow configurable PROMPT path and a warmed, residency-matching hot-standby option (configuration: warm-standby-regions list).
- Evidence bundle size vs run-time latency: collection is asynchronous; gating decision uses a lightweight signed marker then streams bundle post-facto to evidence store to avoid increasing failover latency.
- Operational complexity: add guardrails and operator runbooks that surface the minimal set of decisions to approve automated failovers.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: residency_gate_evaluations{result=ALLOW|BLOCK|PROMPT|QUARANTINE}, evidence_bundle_created, evidence_bundle_signed_latency_seconds, evidence_bundle_upload_success, retention_violation_count.
- Dashboards: per-customer residency compliance view, incident timeline with evidence bundle link, cost + latency impact of quarantine.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag RPE and failover gating (private customers only) behind an admin config.
2) Deploy evidence bundle generator as a separate service with limited retention (30d) to validate format and signing.
3) Run synthetic failover tests in staging and a canary subset of non-critical private customers.
4) Full enablement after legal sign-off and successful audits of synthetic evidence bundles.

Notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration and evidence plumbing; downstream UI/Console work and long-term retention policies will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: RPE returns deterministic decision for any candidate failover target within 50ms median latency
Automatic failover to a region that violates explicit customer residency settings is blocked unless operator PROMPT-approved
Evidence bundle is produced for every residency-impacting action and is SHA256+HSM-signed and available in evidence store within 5 minutes
Evidence bundle contains: routing trace, model version digest, instance IDs, KMS key descriptors, retention policy snapshot, operator decision log
Console shows a per-customer residency incident link that opens the evidence bundle and playbook
Automated tests simulate region loss and validate that warm-standby behavior preserves residency when configured
Unit/integration tests for gating logic and signing are included and reviewed in a GitHub PR
updates: 2025-03-04: Kickoff meeting with Legal (S. Patel) and Platform Security (D. Nguyen) — high-level alignment on evidence schema and KMS key custody. Action: legal to draft minimum required fields for attestations.

2025-03-07: Spike completed for policy engine prototypes (proof-of-concept using OPA-like expression evaluation). Found median latency 18ms for simple rule sets. (note: complex multi-tenant policy trees may exceed 50ms; will add caching layer)
2025-03-10: Design review with SRE and Console teams. Decision: evidence bundles will be uploaded asynchronously; gating will use a signed 'decision token' to avoid adding failover latency.
2025-03-12: Security review kickoff scheduled. Pending: HSM key lifecycle doc and key rotation approach. Assigned to D. Nguyen.
2025-03-14: Created initial GitHub PR #3421 with RPE scaffolding and unit tests. Needs integration tests and Confluence spec linkage before code review.
risks: Availability regression if operators misconfigure strict-block policies; mitigated by PROMPT mode and warm-standby plumbing
Large evidence bundles could increase storage costs and retention complexity; mitigated by compression and retention lifecycle rules
Key compromise risk; requires HSM-backed signing and documented key rotation/escrow procedures
Complexity of multi-tenant policies could increase policy evaluation latency; mitigated by caching and policy compilation
